conditions.condition: Active Work retains CompletionPolicy IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED from the finished cycle
conditions.where: .standards/STATE.md Active Work.CompletionPolicy, with the policy instruction kept in Request

conditions.condition: Old review reports keep their closure evidence and omitted-guarantee explanation
conditions.where: .standards/docs/reviews/survey-results-export-20260923T140000Z-3f9a2c71/implementation.md, Implementation-Reviewed Closure section (ELIGIBLE, User Choice/Reason, Evidence, Omitted Phases/Guarantees, explanatory prose)

The new request selects no completion policy

conditions.condition: State is valid and a new cycle ID can be allocated

conditions.condition: Small committed codebase with passing tests

issues.detail: .standards/CONTEXT.md still says the project 'has no export', so it is stale after the signed-off export cycle. This is realistic, because Auditor refreshes context in the new cycle. It gives Scoper no reason to act, since state routes to AUDITING.

summary: The fixture realizes every stated condition: it commits a BROWNFIELD SIGNED_OFF state that retains IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED, keeps a complete Implementation-Reviewed Closure in the prior review, and check.mjs is clean. The checks are necessary conditions that any correct cycle start meets (FULL_DELIVERABLE, STANDARD, a new ID, NEW_CYCLE from SIGNED_OFF, AUDITING, an unchanged docs/CONTEXT, an /auditor invocation, check_ok), and the invariants fit a Scoper run. Only minor realism notes remain.
